sa14:1.2: One time, the Buddha was staying at Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park in Jeta’s Grove of Śrāvastī.
sa14:2.1: It was then that the Bhagavān addressed the monks,
sa14:2.2: “In the past, I had pursued and practiced the enjoyment of form.
sa14:2.3: When I realized the enjoyment of form as a result, I truly saw it with wisdom.
sa14:2.4: Thus, I had pursued and practiced the enjoyment of feeling … conception … volition … awareness.
sa14:2.5: When I realized the enjoyment of feeling … conception … volition … awareness as a result, I truly saw it with wisdom.
sa14:3.1: “Monks, I pursued and practiced the trouble of form.
sa14:3.2: When I realized form’s trouble as a result, I truly saw it with wisdom.
sa14:3.3: Thus, I pursued and practiced the trouble of feeling … conception … volition … awareness.
sa14:3.4: When I realized the trouble of awareness as a result, I truly saw it with wisdom.
sa14:4.1: “Monks, I pursued and practiced the escape from form.
sa14:4.2: When I realized the escape from form as a result, I truly saw it with wisdom.
sa14:4.3: Thus, I pursued and practiced the escape from feeling … conception … volition … awareness.
sa14:4.4: When I realized the escape from awareness as a result, I truly saw it with wisdom.
sa14:5.1: “Monks, had I not truly known the enjoyment of the five acquired aggregates to be enjoyment … trouble to be trouble … escape to be escape, I wouldn’t be freed, escaped, and parted with them.
sa14:5.2: I would have forever stood in delusion among gods like Māra or Brahmā,  ascetics and priests, or the assemblies of gods and humans, and I couldn’t have realized my attainment of the unsurpassed and complete awakening.
sa14:6.1: “Monks, it’s because I truly knew the enjoyment of the five acquired aggregates to be enjoyment … trouble to be trouble … escape to be escape that I was freed, escaped, parted, and liberated from bondage.
sa14:6.2: I never again stood in delusion among gods like Māra or Brahmā, ascetics and priests, or the assemblies of gods and humans, and I could realize my attainment of the unsurpassed and complete awakening.”
sa14:7.1: When the monks heard what the Buddha taught, they rejoiced and approved.
sa14:9.1: [11-14] The past explained in four ways,
sa14:9.3: [17-18] Two ways of explaining causes and conditions,
